translations.text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes scattered abroad: greetings!
Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various kinds of trials;
know that this testing of your faith produces patience,
and let patience have its perfect work, so that you may be perfect and wholly alive, lacking in nothing.
If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all freely and reproaches no one, and he will give it to him.
But let him ask in faith and without doubting; for whoever doubts is like a wave of the sea, stirred up and tossed about by the wind.
So let that man not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord.
A double-minded man is unstable in all his ways.
Let the lowly brother boast in his exaltation,
and the rich man in his humiliation, for like a flower of the field, so he will pass away.
The sun rose with its heat and withered the grass, and its flower fell, and the beauty of its appearance perished. So too the rich man will fade away in his going.
Blessed is the man who endures trial, for he will be proved and will receive the crown of life, which he promised to those who love him.
Let no one who is tempted say, "I am tempted by God", for God cannot be tempted by evil, and he tempts no one.
Rather, each person is tempted by his own desire, being drawn away and compelled.
Then desire conceives and gives birth to sin, and sin, when it is complete, brings forth death.
Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers!
Every good thing given and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of light, with whom there is no change, nor the fault of a shadow of turning.
By his will he brought us to birth through the word of truth, so that we might be a kind of beginning of his creatures.
Know this now, my beloved brothers: let every man be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger.
For the anger of man does not accomplish the righteousness of God.
Therefore put away all filthiness and the excess of wickedness, and receive with meekness the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
And be doers of the word, and not hearers who bring contempt upon themselves.
If anyone is only a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man who looks at the face of his own form in a mirror.
For he looked at himself and went away, and at once forgot what he was like.
But whoever has looked into the perfect law of freedom and remained in it, not becoming one who forgets but a doer of the work, he will be blessed in his doing.
Whoever thinks himself a servant of God and does not bridle his tongue, but deceives his own heart, his service is vain.
Service that is holy and undefiled before God and the Father is this: to look after orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself undefiled by the world.
My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with partiality.
If a man comes into your assembly wearing a gold ring and shining clothes, and a poor man also comes in wearing filthy clothes,
and you pay attention to the one who wears the shining clothes and say to him, "You sit here in a good place," and to the poor man you say, "You stand there," or "Sit under my feet,"
then you have become divided in your hearts and have become judges with evil thoughts in your hearts.
Listen, my beloved brothers: has not God chosen the poor of the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom which God promised to those who love him?
But you have dishonored the poor man. Is it not the rich who oppress you, and is it not they who drag you before the judge?
Is it not they who blaspheme the good name that is called over you?
If you fulfill the royal law according to the scripture, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself," you do well.
But if you show partiality, you commit sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors of the law.
Whoever fulfills the whole law but stumbles in one point has become liable for all of it.
For he who said, "Do not commit adultery," also said, "Do not kill." If you do not commit adultery but you kill, you have still become a transgressor of the law.
So speak and so act as those who are to be judged by the law of freedom.
For judgment is without mercy to the one who has not shown mercy; but boast in mercy over judgment.
What profit is there, my brothers, if someone says, "I have faith," but has no works? Faith alone cannot save him.
If a brother or a sister is naked and lacks daily food,
and one of you says to them, "Go in peace, be warmed and be filled," but you give them nothing of what the body needs, what profit is that?
So it is with faith also: if it has no works, it is dead by itself.
But someone may say, "You have faith and I have works." Show me your faith without your works, and I will show you my faith by my works.
You believe that God is one; you do well. The demons also believe that, and they tremble before him.
Do you want to know, O empty man, that faith without works is empty?
Abraham our father was justified by works, for he offered up Isaac his son on the altar.
Do you see that faith worked together with his works, and that by works his faith was made perfect?
And the scripture was fulfilled which says, "Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness," and he was called the friend of God.
Do you see now that a person is justified by works, and not by faith alone?
In the same way Rahab the harlot was justified by works, because she took in the spies and sent them away by another road.
Just as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead too.
My brothers, do not let many of you be teachers! Know that you will receive the greater judgment.
For we all go badly wrong. Whoever does not go wrong in speech is a perfect man. He is able to bridle his whole body.
If we put bridles on a horse to make it obey us, we turn its whole body,
Look, ships too, so very large and driven here and there by fierce winds, are turned by a small rudder wherever the steersman wants to go.
In the same way the tongue is a small member, and it boasts greatly. Look, again it sets things on fire!

And the tongue is likewise a fire, the adornment of falsehood. The tongue is set among our members. It defiles the whole body and sets on fire the wheel of creation, and it is itself set on fire by Gehenna.
For every kind of beast and bird, creeping thing and swimming creature can be tamed, and has been tamed by humankind.
But no human being is able to tame the tongue. It is an evil that cannot be restrained, full of deadly poison.
For with it we bless God and the Father, and with the same tongue we curse people, who are made in the likeness of God.
Blessing and cursing come out of the same mouth. My brothers, it is not right for this to be so.
Does a spring pour out sweet and bitter water from the same opening?
My brothers, can a fig tree bear olives, or a vine bear figs? In the same way, salt water cannot become sweet either.
Who among you is wise and understanding? Let him show his work through good conduct, in the gentleness of wisdom.
If you have bitter envy and strife in your hearts, do not boast and speak about the truth.
This is not wisdom that has come down from above. It is earthly, unspiritual and devilish.
Where there is envy and strife, there is disorder and every [?] deed.
But the wisdom from above is first of all purity, then peace, kindness and obedience. It is full of mercy and of the fruit of good works, impartial and free of duplicity.
The fruit of righteousness and peace is sown in peace by those who make peace.
Where do the wars and quarrels among you come from? Do they not come from your own desires, which are at war in your members?
You desire and do not have. You kill and envy, and you cannot obtain. You quarrel and fight, and you do not have, because you do not ask.
You ask and do not receive, because you ask wrongly, so that you may spend it on your desires.
Adulterers, do you not know that love of this world is enmity with God? Whoever wants to be a friend of this world sets himself up as an enemy against God.
Or do you think that the scripture speaks in vain: "The spirit that dwells in us yearns enviously"?
Rather, it gives more grace. That is why it says: "God crushes the proud, but gives grace to the humble."
Submit to God and resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and set your hearts straight, you double-minded.
Humble yourselves and weep. Let your laughter be turned into mourning and your joy into sorrow.
Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you.

Do not speak evil of one another, my brothers. Whoever speaks evil of a brother or judges his brother judges the law and condemns the law. If you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge.
There is one lawgiver and judge, who is able to save and to destroy. Who are you to judge your neighbour?
Now you also who say: "Today or tomorrow let us go to some city, spend a year there, trade and make a profit".
You do not know what tomorrow will bring. How long, then, is your life? You are like smoke, which appears for a little while and then vanishes.
Instead, you ought to say: "If the Lord wills, and we live, we will do this or that."
But now you boast in your arrogance. All such boasting is evil.
Whoever knows the good he ought to do and does not do it, for him it is sin.
Now you also who are rich, weep and wail for the miseries that are coming upon you.
Your wealth has rotted, and moths have eaten your clothing.
Your gold and your silver have corroded, and their corrosion will be a witness against you and will eat your flesh like fire. You have stored up treasure in the last days.
See, the wages of the labourers who reaped your fields, which you held back, cry out, and the cries of the reapers have reached the ears of the Lord Almighty.
You lived in luxury on the earth and took your pleasure. You fattened your flesh as for a day of slaughter.
You condemned and killed the righteous one, and he did not resist you.
Be patient, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. See, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth and is patient over it until it receives the early and the late rain.
You also be patient. Strengthen your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is near.
Do not grumble against one another, my brothers, so that you may not be judged. See, the judge is standing at the doors.
My brothers, as an example of suffering hardship and of patience, remember the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
See, we call blessed those who endured. You have heard of the endurance of Job, and you have seen the end the Lord brought about, for the Lord is very merciful and kind.
Above all, my brothers, do not swear oaths, neither by heaven, nor by earth, nor by any other oath. Let your yes be yes and your no be no, so that you do not fall into double-mindedness.
If any of you is in distress, let him pray; if anyone is cheerful, let him sing.
If anyone is sick, let him call the elders of the church, and let one pray for him and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord.
And the prayer of faith will save the sick person, and the Lord will raise him up. And if he has committed any sin, it will be forgiven him.
Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, so that you may be healed. The supplication of a righteous person is very powerful and helpful.
Elijah was a man like us, and he prayed that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the earth for three years and six months.
And then he prayed again, and the sky gave rain, and the earth brought forth its fruit.
My brothers, if anyone among you strays from the way of truth and someone turns him back,
let them know that whoever turns a sinner back from the way of his error will save a soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins.
